captions.text: c. 1000 BC: Bit Adini is established.
c. 1000 BC: Kush emerges at Napata.

c. 1000 BC: the Sabines settled the central Apennines 'around the tenth century BC', founding Reate, Trebula Mutuesca and Cures Sabini; they 'also inhabited Latium north of the Anio before the founding of Rome'.
c. 1000 BCE: the kingdom of Sindhu and Sauvira stands on the lower Indus.
Dong Son bronze age: the Lac Viet of the Red River.
Babylonia shrinks to its core in Cliopatria's -1000 shape.
c. 1000 BCE: Greeks from the mainland settle the Anatolian coast.
c. 1000 BCE: Greek-speaking Cyprus is drawn with the Greek world on Cliopatria's date.
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): David unites Judah and Israel.
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): Philistia becomes a client state.
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): Moab becomes a client state of David (page: Philistia, Moab, Edom and Ammon became client states; no year).
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): Ammon becomes a client state of David; Saul had already led an army to victory over the Ammonites (no year).
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): Edom becomes a client state of David (no year on the page).
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): Aram-Zobah and Aram-Damascus become vassals of David (page: no year); the Aram-Damascus page places battles between David's Israel and the Arameans in the 10th century BCE.
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): David's Israel takes the inland Philistine lands.
c. 1000 BC (bridged): David makes Moab tributary.
c. 1000 BCE: the culture spreads east into the western Ganga valley.
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): David's Israel takes the northern Philistine lands.
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): Philistia becomes a client of David's Israel.
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): the southern end of the inland strip leaves Philistia without passing to Israel.
1000 BCE: the Late Tichitt phase.
25,192 km2 core: Nabu-shum-libur's dynasty was "deposed by marauding Arameans in 1026 BC" and Arameans and Suteans settled Babylonia "during the 11th century BC"; the page gives no land lost.
19,288 km2 at Susa for -1000..-901: the dark age; the shrinkage to Susa fits 'obscurity' but no page supports or denies it. Unverified: page silent.
c. 975 BC (bridged): the Great Kingdom ends.
c. 975 BC: the Great Kingdom becomes the ordinary Neo-Hittite kingdom of the House of Suhi.
c. 950 BC: Gurgum's first recorded event.
943: Shoshenq I founds the Twenty-second Dynasty.

943: the Twenty-first Dynasty ends and the priests' rule ends with it. The High Priest of Amun page ends the priestly rule at "c. 943 BC" ("effectively the rulers of Upper Egypt from 1080 to c. 943 BC") and the table's last entry, Psusennes III, runs to 943; Iuput, a son of Shoshenq I, is high priest from 944.
943: the priest-kings of Thebes end.
943: the dynasty ends and with it its nominal overlordship of Thebes.
943: the Twenty-first Dynasty gives way to Shoshenq I's Twenty-second.
943: Middle and Upper Egypt pass from the Theban priests' orbit to Shoshenq I (assumed).
934 BC: Ashur-dan II begins the recovery.
c. 931 BCE: the northern kingdom's capital is Shechem.
c. 930: Judah splits from Israel.
c. 930 BCE: Jeroboam's Revolt divides the kingdom.
c. 930 BCE (bridged): the client relation ends with the division; the page gives no date.
c. 930 BCE (bridged): the client relation ends with the division; the Mesha Stele (c. 840 BCE) records Moab as Israel's enemy.
c. 930 BCE (bridged): the client relation ends with the division.
c. 930 BCE (bridged): the client relation ends with the division.
c. 930 BCE (bridged): the vassalage ends with the division; Aram-Damascus then emerges as a rival (Aram-Damascus page).
c. 930: Israel and Judah at war.

c. 930: the founding event's region 'Judea' (Hebron to the Samaria hills, 32.46 N) takes Israeli cells that Judah's own keyframe then drops, leaving six cells round Shechem and Samaria owned by nobody.
c. 931 BC (bridged): Moab is lost to Israel after Solomon.
c. 930 BCE (bridged): the client relation ends when the united monarchy divides.
Judah's core as the page draws its frontier: from the north-western shore of the Dead Sea past Jericho to Gezer, across the Shephelah to Beersheba in the north Negev; the -900 shape unchanged
By 920 BC: Sam'al is a kingdom.

912 BC: the Middle Assyrian Empire ends with the death of Ashur-dan II; the Neo-Assyrian Empire is counted from 911 (accession of Adad-nirari II). Same state, same family: successor in the next dossier.
911 BC: Adad-nirari II becomes king of Assyria and the Neo-Assyrian Empire begins.
c. 911: end of the fighting, bridged to the end of Abijah's reign.
c. 909 BCE: the capital moves to Tirzah (infobox: Tirzah c. 909–880).

conflicts.rule: ruling of data/patches/m1000-m0901.json: rulings/0: The 60 km Carchemish disc (and the 90 km one before -975) lies over Bit Adini's disc and the size rule gave the capital's land to Carchemish from -975, leaving Bit Adini a crescent. The page: Bit Adini is 'usually thought to have been in the bend of the Euphrates River, south of Carchemish', 'with its capital at Til Barsip (now Tell Ahmar)'. South of Carchemish's latitude the land goes to Bit Adini, north of it the size rule stands. The line is an approximation: the page gives no frontier. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: the city's own cell (centre 36.77 N) lay inside the polygon and went to Bit Adini from -1000 to the end of the window; carved out with a 10 km disc. North of the line the size rule gave Bit Adini (the smaller claim) Carchemish itself in -1000..-976; rulings/2 gives those cells to Carchemish.] (found)

ruling of data/patches/m1000-m0901.json: rulings/2: Companion to rulings/0 (added by the reviewer, 2 Nov 2026): Carchemish itself and its district north of the city's latitude stay Carchemish's. Bit Adini's 70 km disc is smaller than Carchemish's 90 km disc of -1175..-976, so the size rule gave Bit Adini the city of Carchemish for 25 years; the page puts Bit Adini 'in the bend of the Euphrates River, south of Carchemish', 'one of the two chief states of the Aramean-held territories in the Euphrates along with Carchemish'. The outer ring east of the Euphrates (between it and the Balikh, where the page also puts Bit Adini) is left to the size rule. From -975 Carchemish's 60 km disc is the smaller claim and the size rule already decides the same way. (found)

ruling of data/patches/m1000-m0901.json: rulings/1: The Nile Valley region of the Theban priests (and of the Twenty-second Dynasty after them) runs down the whole Aswan governorate to the Sudan border, so 42 cells south of the first cataract, inside Kush's -1000 shape (bbox from 23.8 N), went to the Egyptian side by the size rule and cut a strip of Egypt through Lower Nubia. The page: Kush 'referred to the region south of the first cataract in general', 'the first cataract at Elephantine usually being considered the traditional border between the two polities'; 'With the disintegration of the New Kingdom around 1070 BC ... Kush became an independent kingdom centered at Napata'; Kashta, in the 8th century BC, was the one who 'extended Kushite control north to Elephantine and Thebes'. The page gives no early border of its own (silent on c. 1000-900), so the traditional border at the cataract stands: the contested cells south of it are Kush's. (found)

ruling of data/patches/m1000-m0901.json: rulings/2: Companion to rulings/0 (added by the reviewer, 2 Nov 2026): Carchemish itself and its district north of the city's latitude stay Carchemish's. Bit Adini's 70 km disc is smaller than Carchemish's 90 km disc of -1175..-976, so the size rule gave Bit Adini the city of Carchemish for 25 years; the page puts Bit Adini 'in the bend of the Euphrates River, south of Carchemish', 'one of the two chief states of the Aramean-held territories in the Euphrates along with Carchemish'. The outer ring east of the Euphrates (between it and the Balikh, where the page also puts Bit Adini) is left to the size rule.
